country.name: Slovakia
country.tagline: Little Carpathian royal towns, Danube plain reds and a slice of Tokaj that both sides of the border claim.

stats.note: Statistical Office of the Slovak Republic via FAOSTAT (official figure): 9,000 ha of vines in 2024; about 10,000 ha were worked in 2011 (SITA), against up to 57,000 ha in the early nineteenth century. No current production figure found

country.overview:
Slovakia's vineyards lie along its southern edge, from the foothills of the Little Carpathians above Bratislava to the volcanic hills of Tokaj on the Hungarian and Ukrainian borders, and cover about 9,000 hectares (2024) in six wine regions. For most of history this was Upper Hungary, and in the early nineteenth century the area supplied wine to European courts from as much as 57,000 hectares; phylloxera, war and four decades of state cooperatives shrank and flattened the industry, and the modern revival dates from the 1990s.

The Little Carpathians (Malokarpatská) are the historic heart, with the old royal free towns of Svätý Jur, Pezinok and Modra, where burgher families made wine in courtyards and cellars under their houses, and Bratislava's Rača district, famous for Frankovka. The Danube plain to the south-east (Južnoslovenská) and the hills around Nitra (Nitrianska) give fuller, riper whites and reds, and the smaller Central and East Slovak regions add volcanic and loess sites. Grüner Veltliner and Welschriesling are the most planted grapes, with Blaufränkisch, Müller-Thurgau, Saint Laurent, Pinot Blanc and Riesling. Slovak breeders, notably Dorota Pospíšilová, created crossings such as Devín (white) and Dunaj (red) that are now local favourites.

Slovakia's corner of Tokaj, seven villages around Malá Tŕňa and Viničky, makes the same botrytised wines as Hungarian Tokaj, from Furmint, Lipovina (Hárslevelű) and Yellow Muscat, under the name Tokajský výber. Hungary fought for years to stop Slovakia using the name; EU courts rejected Hungary's challenge in 2012 and 2013, and both countries now use it.

history.title: Romans on the Danube limes
history.text: Roman forts such as Gerulata (Bratislava-Rusovce) guarded the Danube, and Emperor Probus is traditionally credited with spreading vines in Pannonia.

history.title: Royal free towns of wine
history.text: Modra, Svätý Jur and Pezinok became royal free towns of the Kingdom of Hungary in the seventeenth century, status bought with the wealth of their wine trade.

history.title: Trianon splits Tokaj
history.text: The Treaty of Trianon left three Tokaj villages and about 175 ha in Czechoslovakia; later laws added villages up to the present seven and about 908 ha.

history.title: The Tokaj dispute
history.text: A 2004 agreement allowed Slovak wine from 565 ha to use the Tokaj name under Hungarian-style rules; Hungary later sought to remove Slovakia's 'Vinohradnícka oblasť Tokaj' from the EU register, but the General Court (2012) and Court of Justice (2013) rejected its case.

country.classification: Slovak wine follows EU categories. Five regional PDOs (Malokarpatská, Južnoslovenská, Nitrianska, Stredoslovenská, Východoslovenská) and the Vinohradnícka oblasť Tokaj PDO are registered, each with grammatical variants; two more local PDOs are Karpatská perla (2011, a quality label for the Bratislava and Little Carpathian area) and Skalický rubín (2017, a red blend from Skalica). Quality wines with a predicate follow the German ladder (kabinetné, neskorý zber, výber z hrozna, bobuľový výber, hrozienkový výber, cibébový výber, ľadové víno, slamové víno). Special terms include mladé víno (young wine sold from the first Monday in November), archívne víno (aged three years) and panenská úroda (first harvest of a new vineyard).
country.climate_soils: Continental with warm summers. The Little Carpathians have granite and schist on the slopes and loess below; the Danube plain has sand, gravel and loess; Nitra and Central Slovakia have loess, clay and volcanic andesite in places; Tokaj and the East have volcanic tuff, andesite and loess.

grapes.name: Grüner Veltliner (Veltlínske zelené)
grapes.note: The most planted grape, about 3,700 ha.

grapes.name: Blaufränkisch (Frankovka modrá)
grapes.note: The main red, about 1,800 ha, famous at Rača.

grapes.name: Müller-Thurgau, Saint Laurent, Pinot Blanc, Riesling
Devín, Dunaj, Hetera
grapes.note: Slovak crossings; Devín is aromatic white, Dunaj a deep red.

regions.name: Malokarpatská
regions.tagline: Royal wine towns on the slopes above Bratislava.
regions.summary: The Little Carpathian region runs north-east from Bratislava along the foothills, through Rača, Svätý Jur, Pezinok and Modra to Trnava and Skalica, and is Slovakia's most historic and largest wine region. Courtyard wineries, the annual Open Cellar days and the Little Carpathian Wine Route link the towns; Rača's Frankovka, Pezinok's Grüner and Riesling and Modra's research station (home of Slovak grape breeding) are its pillars.
regions.history: Vines were grown on these slopes under the Romans and in the Middle Ages by German-speaking settlers; Svätý Jur, Pezinok and Modra grew rich on wine and became royal free towns of the Kingdom of Hungary in the seventeenth century. Under communism the large state cooperatives dominated; family wineries returned after 1989.
regions.terroir: Granite and crystalline schist on the slopes, loess and alluvium below; sheltered from north winds by the mountains.
regions.grapes: Grüner Veltliner, Welschriesling, Blaufränkisch, Müller-Thurgau, Saint Laurent, Riesling, Pinot Blanc, Devín
regions.styles: Dry whites, reds, rosé, Prädikat wines

sources.title: Candiago et al. (2022), geospatial inventory of EU wine PDOs (registration dates, varieties, communes)

regions.name: Južnoslovenská
regions.tagline: The warm Danube plain, rich whites and reds.
regions.summary: The South Slovak region spreads across the Danube lowland from Šamorín and Dunajská Streda to Galanta, Komárno, Strekov and Štúrovo, largely in the Hungarian-speaking south. It is warm and dry, giving ripe whites and reds; Château Belá near Štúrovo, run with the Saar's Egon Müller, made Slovak Riesling internationally known.
regions.history: The Danube plain was part of Hungary's wine economy for centuries; Strekov and Štúrovo (opposite Esztergom) have medieval roots. Modern investment since the 1990s, including Château Belá, revived quality.
regions.terroir: Sand, gravel and loess on the plain, with loess and clay hills near Strekov and Štúrovo.
regions.grapes: Grüner Veltliner, Welschriesling, Blaufränkisch, Müller-Thurgau, Saint Laurent, Riesling, Pinot Blanc, Devín
regions.styles: Dry whites, reds, rosé, Prädikat wines

sources.title: Candiago et al. (2022), geospatial inventory of EU wine PDOs (registration dates, varieties, communes)

regions.name: Nitrianska
regions.tagline: Loess hills around the old capital of Nitra.
regions.summary: The Nitra region is the largest by area, around Nitra, Hlohovec, Zlaté Moravce, Vráble and Topoľčianky, with loess hills and some volcanic sites in the south-east. Château Topoľčianky, in the Habsburg estate town with its national stud, is a major producer.
regions.history: Nitra, seat of a Great Moravian prince and Slovakia's oldest town, has a wine history going back over a thousand years; Topoľčianky was a Habsburg estate.
regions.terroir: Loess and clay, with andesite near the Štiavnica hills.
regions.grapes: Grüner Veltliner, Welschriesling, Blaufränkisch, Müller-Thurgau, Saint Laurent, Riesling, Pinot Blanc, Devín
regions.styles: Dry whites, reds, rosé, Prädikat wines

sources.title: Candiago et al. (2022), geospatial inventory of EU wine PDOs (registration dates, varieties, communes)

regions.name: Stredoslovenská
regions.tagline: Small vineyards of the southern central hills.
regions.summary: The Central Slovak region lies along the Hungarian border around Modrý Kameň, Fiľakovo, Rimavská Sobota and Tornaľa, with scattered vineyards on loess and volcanic soils.
regions.history: Small peasant vineyards in the Hungarian-speaking south, long overshadowed by neighbouring Eger and Tokaj across the border.
regions.terroir: Loess, clay and volcanic rock; warm summers.
regions.grapes: Grüner Veltliner, Welschriesling, Blaufränkisch, Müller-Thurgau, Saint Laurent, Riesling, Pinot Blanc, Devín
regions.styles: Dry whites, reds, rosé, Prädikat wines

sources.title: Candiago et al. (2022), geospatial inventory of EU wine PDOs (registration dates, varieties, communes)

regions.name: Východoslovenská
regions.tagline: Volcanic hills of the east, next to Tokaj.
regions.summary: The East Slovak region covers vineyards around Košice, Moldava nad Bodvou and the Trebišov and Michalovce areas outside the Tokaj delimitation, on volcanic and loess soils.
regions.history: Viticulture around Košice and the Zemplín shares its history with Tokaj; the region was cut off from Hungarian markets after 1920.
regions.grapes: Grüner Veltliner, Welschriesling, Blaufränkisch, Müller-Thurgau, Saint Laurent, Riesling, Pinot Blanc, Devín
regions.styles: Dry whites, reds, rosé, Prädikat wines

regions.name: Tokaj (Slovakia)
regions.tagline: Seven villages of volcanic Tokaj on the Slovak side of the border.
regions.summary: Slovak Tokaj covers about 908 hectares of classified vineyards in seven villages of the Trebišov district (Bara, Čerhov, Černochov, Malá Tŕňa, Slovenské Nové Mesto, Veľká Tŕňa and Viničky), on the northern edge of the Zemplén hills that form Hungarian Tokaj. The same grapes (Furmint, Lipovina and Yellow Muscat) and the same botrytis styles are made, including Tokajský výber, graded in puttony, and Tokajská esencia. Medieval cellars cut into volcanic tuff riddle the hills of Malá Tŕňa and Veľká Tŕňa.
regions.history: The region was split from Hungarian Tokaj by the Treaty of Trianon in 1920. The long dispute over the name was settled in Slovakia's favour by EU courts in 2012 and 2013.
regions.terroir: Volcanic tuff, andesite and loess on south-facing slopes above the Bodrog plain; autumn mists from the Bodrog and Latorica bring noble rot.
regions.styles: Dry and sweet Tokaj wines, samorodné, výber (aszú), esencia, mášláš, fordítáš.

sk-juznoslovenska.name: Južnoslovenská / Južnoslovenské / Južnoslovenský
sk-juznoslovenska.grapes: Grüner Veltliner, Welschriesling, Blaufränkisch, Müller-Thurgau, Saint Laurent, Riesling, Pinot Blanc, Devín and others
sk-juznoslovenska.summary: The South Slovak PDO (EU reg. 2006) for the Danube plain, 120 municipalities from Šamorín to Štúrovo. Warm, dry and sandy, it gives ripe whites and reds; Strekov and Belá have become sources of some of the country's most talked-about wines.
sk-juznoslovenska.nerd_note: Château Belá's Riesling, made with Egon Müller of the Saar, put Slovakia on serious wine lists from the early 2000s.

sk-karpatska-perla.name: Karpatská perla
sk-karpatska-perla.summary: Karpatská perla ('Carpathian pearl') is a PDO registered in 2011 for 34 municipalities of Bratislava and the Little Carpathian foothills, used as a tasting-controlled quality label for local wines. Not to be confused with the producer Karpatská Perla in Šenkvice.
sk-karpatska-perla.terroir: Granite and loess of the Little Carpathian foothills.

sk-malokarpatska.name: Malokarpatská / Malokarpatské / Malokarpatský
sk-malokarpatska.grapes: Grüner Veltliner, Welschriesling, Blaufränkisch, Müller-Thurgau, Saint Laurent, Riesling, Pinot Blanc, Devín and others
sk-malokarpatska.summary: The Little Carpathian PDO (EU reg. 2006), covering 143 municipalities from Bratislava to Skalica. It includes the wine towns of Rača, Svätý Jur, Pezinok and Modra, whose burghers made the region's fortune, and modern producers who have revived Grüner Veltliner, Riesling and Frankovka from granite slopes.
sk-malokarpatska.nerd_note: Rača in Bratislava has been famous for Frankovka (Blaufränkisch) for centuries; its annual harvest festival celebrates the grape.

sk-nitrianska.name: Nitrianska / Nitrianske / Nitriansky
sk-nitrianska.grapes: Grüner Veltliner, Welschriesling, Blaufränkisch, Müller-Thurgau, Saint Laurent, Riesling, Pinot Blanc, Devín and others
sk-nitrianska.summary: The Nitra PDO (EU reg. 2006), the largest Slovak region by municipalities (192), around Nitra, Hlohovec, Zlaté Moravce and Vráble. Loess hills give balanced whites and reds; Château Topoľčianky is a key producer.

sk-skalicky-rubin.name: Skalický rubín
sk-skalicky-rubin.summary: Skalický rubín ('Skalica ruby') is a traditional red blend from six municipalities around Skalica in the far west of Slovakia, near the Moravian border, registered as a PDO in 2017. It must blend Frankovka modrá, Modrý Portugal and Svätovavrinecké, revived from a nineteenth-century local tradition.
sk-skalicky-rubin.terroir: Loess and sand at the foot of the White Carpathians.
sk-skalicky-rubin.nerd_note: One of the few PDOs defined by a specific red blend of three grapes.

sk-stredoslovenska.name: Stredoslovenská / Stredoslovenský / Stredoslovenské
sk-stredoslovenska.grapes: Grüner Veltliner, Welschriesling, Blaufränkisch, Müller-Thurgau, Saint Laurent, Riesling, Pinot Blanc, Devín and others
sk-stredoslovenska.summary: The Central Slovak PDO (EU reg. 2006), 133 municipalities along the southern border around Modrý Kameň, Fiľakovo and Rimavská Sobota, with small family vineyards.

sk-vinohradnicka-oblast-tokaj.name: Vinohradnícka oblasť Tokaj
sk-vinohradnicka-oblast-tokaj.created: 2006 (EU reg.); upheld by EU courts 2012 and 2013
sk-vinohradnicka-oblast-tokaj.summary: The Slovak Tokaj PDO covers seven villages and about 908 hectares of classified vineyards on the northern edge of the Zemplén hills. It makes the full range of Tokaj styles: dry Furmint and Lipovina, samorodné from bunches with botrytised berries, Tokajský výber (the Slovak name for aszú) graded from 3 to 6 puttony, výberová esencia and esencia, plus mášláš and fordítáš made by re-fermenting must on aszú lees. The Hungarian state long argued that only Hungarian wine should bear the name, but after the 2004 bilateral agreement and failed EU court actions in 2012 and 2013, both countries use it. Malá Tŕňa and Veľká Tŕňa, with tuff cellars dating back centuries, are the centre.
sk-vinohradnicka-oblast-tokaj.terroir: Volcanic tuff, andesite and loess; humid autumns from the Bodrog river favour botrytis.
sk-vinohradnicka-oblast-tokaj.nerd_note: Slovak Tokaj producers still nominally follow the Hungarian Tokaj law of 1908 (Law XLVII) for traditional styles.

sk-vychodoslovenska.name: Východoslovenská / Východoslovenský / Východoslovenské
sk-vychodoslovenska.grapes: Grüner Veltliner, Welschriesling, Blaufränkisch, Müller-Thurgau, Saint Laurent, Riesling, Pinot Blanc, Devín and others
sk-vychodoslovenska.summary: The East Slovak PDO (EU reg. 2006), 99 municipalities around Košice, Moldava nad Bodvou and the Zemplín outside the Tokaj delimitation. Volcanic and loess soils near the Tokaj hills give aromatic whites, including Furmint and Lipovina sold without the Tokaj name.

sites.name: Svätý Jur
sites.class: Royal free town of the Little Carpathians
sites.text: A small Little Carpathian town that became a royal free town in the seventeenth century thanks to its wine trade, with burgher houses, courtyard cellars and vineyards climbing to the forest.

sites.name: Pezinok Castle (Zámok Pezinok)
sites.text: A castle in Pezinok, a royal free town since the seventeenth century, whose cellars are used by a winery; the town hosts Little Carpathian wine festivals.

sites.name: Modra
sites.class: Royal free town and seat of Slovak grape research
sites.text: A royal free town since the seventeenth century, famous for its majolica pottery and its vine research station, where Slovak grape crossings were developed.

sites.name: Château Topoľčianky
sites.text: A large winery in Topoľčianky, the Habsburg estate town with its castle and national stud, in the Nitra region.

sites.name: Malá Tŕňa tuff cellars
sites.text: A Slovak Tokaj village whose hillside is riddled with cellars cut into volcanic tuff, including those of Tokaj Macik and other producers.

sites.name: Tokaj Macik Winery
sites.text: One of the leading Slovak Tokaj producers, based in Malá Tŕňa with historic tuff cellars.

sites.name: Viničky
sites.text: The easternmost Slovak Tokaj village, whose name means 'little vineyards', on the edge of the Bodrog plain.

sites.name: Veľká Tŕňa
sites.text: A Tokaj village with long rows of tuff cellars and producers such as J&J Ostrožovič.
